About

A bit about me

I'm an incoming junior studying Mechanical Engineering at UCLA, specializing in safety-critical controls, real-time robotics, and physical mechanical design. My engineering approach has always been rooted in building hardware that works under real-world conditions — modular, reliable, and ready to iterate fast.

I'm driven by two goals: expanding humanity's reach into space, and using engineering to create experiences that spark wonder. Whether that's building scalable spacecraft hardware, designing autonomous robotic systems, or engineering immersive physical experiences that leave people amazed — I want my work to have real impact on real people.

Growing up, my cousin was the only Latino engineer I knew. That gap in representation is part of what drives me — today I'm the only Latino undergraduate in my research lab, and I take that as motivation to deliver, to mentor, and to open doors for the next generation. Sí, se puede.

After my B.S., I plan to pursue a Master's in Electrical and Computer Engineering at UCLA to master the full robotics stack — combining my mechanical foundation with advanced controls and embedded systems. Fluent in English and Spanish. US citizen.
